title: Google: 400 ms search delay reduces usage in weeks four through six

change.variant: Inject a 400 ms server-side delay for six weeks; compare search usage during the second three weeks.

result.metric: searches per user during the second three weeks of a six-week experiment

quote: users exposed to a 400 ms delay since the beginning of the experiment did 0.44% fewer searches during the first three weeks, but 0.76% fewer searches during the second three weeks.
notes: The source reports a range across delays and observation windows, not one overall lift. This record isolates the published 400 ms comparison in weeks four through six; the first three weeks showed 0.44% fewer searches. No pooled lift is inferred.

verification_details.reason: company, lift and supporting quote confirmed; not a statistical replication
